g.text: Please use CSS style instead of skinparam ParticipantPadding
This used to be a correctness problem. It is now a waste problem.
The plan was written against Fitbit, whose refresh tokens were single-use and
rotated: a lost race destroyed a credential and forced a manual re-auth. Neither
Google nor Strava rotates, so a lost race now costs one wasted refresh. The
compare-and-swap stays — it is cheap, and it is what keeps the store's contents
coherent — but do not describe it as load-bearing. See PLAN.md §8.

in the store is what you use.**
Retry the write, never the refresh.
A conflict means someone else already
did the work. Refreshing again on conflict is how a bounded race becomes an
unbounded one. `oauth.TokenHolder` expresses this as a return value: `on_refresh`
